answer: FY26's 7.1% cash-NPAT growth was higher quality on composition than FY25's 4%: operating performance accelerated to 6.5% growth while loan impairment expense increased 8.5% and the loss rate rose to 8bp. FY25 operating performance grew only 3% and benefited from a $76 million impairment decline and a loss-rate fall to 7bp. FY26 income was volume-led, with $1,563 million of incremental NII and $196 million of incremental OOI. Reported NIM compression from 2.08% to 2.05% overstates economic pressure: CBA's bridge shows a 4bp liquids/repo drag with minimal earnings impact, alongside 5bp of asset-pricing pressure offset by 5bp hedging and 2bp mix benefits. The quality improvement is not pristine because OOI included unquantified one-offs, margin pricing remained competitive, and the 8bp impairment-expense ratio is not a through-cycle or realised-loss forecast.

key_facts.fact: FY25 cash NPAT rose 4% to $10,252 million while operating performance rose 3%; loan impairment expense fell $76 million.

citations.quote: Cash net profit after tax (“cash NPAT” or “cash profit”) from continuing operations increased $416 million or 4% on the prior year to $10,252 million.

The result was driven by a 3% increase in operating performance with a 5% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses 2, as well as a $76 million decrease in loan impairment expense.

key_facts.fact: FY25 NII increased $1,199 million or 5%, while other operating income increased $92 million or 2%.

citations.quote: Net interest income was $24,023 million, an increase of $1,199 million or 5% on the prior year.
Other operating income was $4,442 million, an increase of $92 million or 2% on the prior year.

key_facts.fact: FY25 loan impairment expense was $726 million, down 9%, and the loan-loss rate decreased 2 basis points to 7 basis points.

citations.quote: Loan impairment expense was $726 million, a decrease of $76 million or 9% on the prior year.
Loan impairment expense as a percentage of average gross loans and acceptances (GLAAs) decreased 2 basis points to 7 basis points.

key_facts.fact: FY26's operating-income increase comprised $1,563 million of net interest income and $196 million of other operating income.

key_facts.fact: FY25's reported NIM increased 9 basis points to 2.08%, including 7 basis points from lower liquid assets and pooled facilities; excluding that effect, NIM increased 2 basis points.

citations.quote: The Bank’s net interest margin increased 9 basis points on the prior year to 2.08%.

Excluding a 7 basis point increase in margin from a reduction in lower yielding liquid assets and institutional pooled facilities, which have a broadly neutral impact on net interest income, net interest margin increased 2 basis points.

limitations: CBA identifies one-off gains in FY26 other operating income but does not quantify each item separately, so a fully normalised FY26 cash NPAT cannot be derived without estimating.

The margin bridge is a management attribution: the presentation groups institutional repos with liquids, while the profit announcement includes the repo effect within Treasury and Markets; the total NIM movement agrees.
The disclosed loan-loss rate is loan impairment expense divided by average gross loans and acceptances; it is not a through-cycle loss forecast or a direct measure of realised credit losses.
